subject: Minerva Health - retained-debug-traces scope and conditional deletion schedule
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@minervahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: security@minervahealth.com
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Minerva request — retained debug traces for investigational audit

Hi Rafael,

Quick question from our compliance team: for a small subset of production tenants under a regulated trial, we need debug traces (request/response and indexed telemetry) retained for 180 days instead of Redwood's standard 30-day window. This is a scoped ask for three tenant IDs that will be flagged for potential FDA forensics.

Can Redwood provide: 
- confirmation that tenant-level retention overrides are technically possible,
- the evidence package (SOC 2 section on data retention, CAIQ mapping, and any retention-change audit logs), and
- a suggested contractual addendum or attestation we can include for regulators?

Also please call out any operational caveats (performance, TTL backfills, cost uplift). We need to get this documented by next week (target: 2026-09-30) to align with our trial submission.

Thanks,
Carlos
Carlos Vega
Director, IT Compliance
Minerva Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@minervahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minerva request — retained debug traces for investigational audit

Carlos — thanks for the clear ask. We can support a scoped, tenant-level retention override but there are a few policy and operational items to confirm. I looped in Kimberly (security & compliance) and Ben (CS lead) to outline the evidence packet and next steps.

Deliverables I think we'll provide: 
- short attestation template for regulators,
- retention change audit log export (time-stamped),
- CAIQ notes mapping the affected controls, and
- proposed contract addendum language for a time-bound exception.

I attached our high-level data lifecycle doc to this thread for context.

Proposed next step: Kimberly, can you review the scope (3 tenant IDs, 180d, EU region) and confirm whether we need a SOC 2 supplement or a CAIQ tailoring note? Ben — please confirm whether an order/commit or one-off engineering request is needed and ballpark cost impact.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@minervahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minerva request — retained debug traces for investigational audit

Hi all — I reviewed the requested scope. Short answers first: yes, tenant-level TTL overrides are supported via a scoped retention exception workflow; yes, we can produce the evidence listed. Notes and constraints below.

Scope & controls mapping: 
- Default production telemetry/trace retention: 30 days (Redwood-policy-TTL-v3).
- Exception requested: 180 days for three tenant IDs (EU region).
- CAIQ/SIG items impacted: SI-12 (log retention/config), CP-8 (data lifecycle), and AIS-Data-Retention sections. I will produce a CAIQ-tailored-notes PDF showing exact control mappings and compensating controls.

Operational caveats: 
- Storage: 180d will increase token-storage footprint; for small number of tenants impact is modest but measurable.
- Performance: serving runtime unaffected for reads; long-tail retention requires longer index lifecycle which has minor search cost.
- Forensics & chain of custody: we recommend a forensics snapshot (immutable export) on request to accompany the retention override.
- Audit trail: any TTL override is logged and an immutable record is generated (we can export in CSV/JSON).

Contractual/evidence items we can provide: 
- Attestation letter (customized) — attestation-template.docx,
- CAIQ tailored notes — caiq-tailored-notes.pdf,
- Retention exception checklist (technical + legal steps) — retention-exception-checklist.xlsx,
- SOC 2 reference and applicable control mapping (we'll include the SOC 2 report redaction guidance).

Timeline: 
- Draft attestation & CAIQ notes: 2 business days after acceptance of scope,
- Technical implementation (engineer ticket + TTL override): target 3 business days after approval,
- Final evidence packet (full zip): 4 business days.

We will need a signed addendum or an internal purchase order that references the exception to log the change in our compliance register. Rafael/Ben, please confirm deal path.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park | Sr. Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@minervahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minerva request — retained debug traces for investigational audit

Kimberly — this is exactly what we need, thank you. Two follow-ups: 
1) Can you include a one-page signed attestation that explicitly references the three tenant IDs and the 180-day window? We're required to submit signed proof to the study sponsor.
2) Cost: is the TTL override billable as an add-on? If yes, please provide an estimate we can budget into the trial costs.

If you can provide the attestation and a quick cost table by end-of-day tomorrow that would be ideal. We'll prepare a DocuSign package once we have the attestation template.

Best,
Carlos
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@minervahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Minerva request — retained debug traces for investigational audit

Carlos — summary and next steps so we have a single checklist: 
1) Redwood will produce: attestation (signed), CAIQ tailored notes, retention exception checklist, TTL-override audit export. Deliverable ETA: 48 business hours from your written scope approval.
2) Engineering work: Ben, please open an internal ticket to implement the tenant TTL override and schedule the immutable forensics snapshot cadence (on-demand).
3) Costing: Ben to provide a one-line cost estimate for the 180d retention per tenant (storage + operational uplift).
4) Legal/contract: I'll attach the attestation template to the DocuSign envelope once Kimberly confirms wording.
5) Evidence & export: Naomi, can you assemble the SOC 2 reference pages and the CSV export format for the TTL-audit?

Carlos — if that timeline works, reply with a one-line approval of the scoped three tenant IDs and we'll kick off the work.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
